newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan imprisons tycoon for stock default scandal.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan imprisons tycoon for stock default scandal.

text.p: Taiwan has sentenced a tycoon and former politician to four years in prison for stock manipulation and involvement in a share payment default scandal, a court official said on Friday.
"The court orders Oung Ta-ming and his assistant Lee Shou-fan to four years in prison," a spokewoman at the Taipei District Court told Reuters by telephone.
Oung, a former legislator, heads the textile giant Hualon group and is known as the market's most prominent investor.
Oung, who did not run for re-election in December 1995, could not be reached for comment.

The T$3.35 billion ($122 million) stock payment default was a major blow to the island's hypersensitive bourse, leading the weighted stock market index to plunge more than 1,000 points in October 1994.
Of the defaults reported to authorities, T$2.7 billion was by the two Hualon brokerages, which have been closed.
The brokerages issued cheques worth T$200 million that bounced in early October 1994, triggering the share payment default scandal that sent the market plummeting 14.7 percent in just one week.
The scandal was rooted in Hualon's alleged manipulation of speculative counter Imperial Hotel, which surged to a year-high of T$402 in August 1993 from just T$30 in January 1993.
On Friday, the stock market shrugged off the impact of Oung's sentence, rising 0.46 percent to close at 6,890.66 points.
"...The sentence is not a surprise," said Michael Hung, research manager of Nikko Securities.
"The market has disregarded the news and there are rumours that Hualon has entered the market to boost its own share price," Hung added.
Hualon Corp was the session's most active issue on Friday, ending 1.16 percent higher at T$26.2.
"The case is not final. They can still appeal," said Amy Huang, an analyst at Nomura Securities. "Hualon group should enter to support their share price." (T$27.5 = $1)
